title: Better structured logging for region health evaluations
author: Allison Grant
release_notes: Improves region health evaluation logs with structured fields and consistent event naming to speed triage during regional impairments and controlled failover tests.
body: Motivation: During rehearsal + game day prep we repeatedly lost time answering basic questions like “which signal caused the region to be marked impaired?”, “was it corroborated?”, and “what inputs were stale/missing?”. Existing logs were a mix of ad-hoc strings across the region-health service + routing policy evaluation, often without enough structured context to join against traces/alerts. This PR standardizes and enriches structured logs emitted during region health evaluations and policy-engine consumption so on-call can quickly identify the evaluation path and the evidence. Summary of changes: (1) Introduce a consistent event name set for region health evaluation lifecycle: region_health.evaluate.start, region_health.evaluate.signal, region_health.evaluate.result, region_health.evaluate.error. (2) Add structured fields (stable keys) on each event: eval_id (UUID), region, service (hosted|dedicated), route (when applicable), model_family (when applicable), signal_name, signal_source (reachability|burn_rate_5xx|burn_rate_latency|capacity|control_plane), signal_value (normalized), signal_state (ok|degraded|impaired|unknown), corroboration_required (bool), corroboration_met (bool), confidence (0-1), hold_down_ms, ttl_age_ms, cache_hit (bool), missing_inputs (comma-separated), evaluation_version (semantic string), and decision (ok|degrade|failover_recommended). (3) Ensure logs are emitted at the decision points (priority selection + dampening/hold-down) rather than on every internal sub-call; add lightweight debug logs behind a feature flag (REGION_HEALTH_DEBUG_LOGS) for deep dives. (4) Add safe redaction/PII guardrails: do not log tenant_id; when tenant context is required for safety-limit debugging we log tenant_tier and a stable tenant_hash derived from an internal salt (for joinability without disclosure). (5) Add unit tests for log payload shape (golden keys) and error-path coverage (missing signal stream, parse failures). (6) Update runbook snippets in code comments: example queries and how to pivot from burn-rate alert -> evaluation result -> policy flip audit event. Example (after): Search for a single evaluation: event=region_health.evaluate.result eval_id=<id> | fields region, decision, confidence, missing_inputs, hold_down_ms, ttl_age_ms. Identify which signal dominated: event=region_health.evaluate.signal eval_id=<id> | sort by signal_priority asc. Identify unknown due to stale inputs: event=region_health.evaluate.result region=us-east | filter signal_state=unknown OR ttl_age_ms>5000 OR missing_inputs!="". Notes: This PR is intentionally log-only and does not change trigger semantics. It complements PR-19825 (TTL jittering) and PR-19840 (controller NPE on missing signal) by making the remaining “why did it decide that?” questions answerable quickly. Rollout: Safe to ship broadly; log volume increase measured at ~3–5% in staging under normal conditions. Debug logs remain off by default and are sampled (1%) when enabled. Follow-ups: (a) wire eval_id through the failover controller audit events for one-click joins (tracked in ENG-2426), (b) add dashboard annotations from evaluate.result when decision=failover_recommended (INT-1149).
commits: region-health: add structured log events + eval_id propagation
region-health: normalize signal naming + log key schema
routing: include region_health eval_id in policy evaluation logs
logging: add redaction helpers + tenant_hash utility
tests: golden log payload assertions for evaluate.* events
chore: docs-in-code examples for common triage queries
conversation:
Miles Thornton (review): Can we guarantee stable keys across all events? On-call will build saved searches off this. Also, confidence should be explicitly 0..1, not a string.
Allison Grant (author): Yep — added a shared schema helper used by all evaluate.* events; confidence is a float and we clamp to [0,1]. Added unit tests to fail if keys drift.

Ravi Menon (review): Please avoid putting route/model on every event; this will explode cardinality when sampled logs are shipped to the long-retention sink.
Allison Grant (author): Agreed. Updated to only include route/model_family on evaluate.result (and only when policy-engine requests tenant/route-scoped evaluation). Signal-level events remain region-scoped.

Sergio Costa (review): Can we include ttl_age_ms and cache_hit? The last incident we suspected stale reachability inputs.
Allison Grant (author): Added ttl_age_ms/cache_hit to signal + result events; also added missing_inputs field when any required stream is absent.

Victor Alvarez (review): For reachability failures, I want to distinguish “probe timed out” vs “DNS resolution” vs “TCP connect refused”.
Allison Grant (author): Added reachability_error_class (dns|tcp|tls|timeout|http|unknown) only on reachability signal events; mapped from perf-canary probe status.

Miles Thornton (follow-up): Please add an example query to join evaluate.result to the routing decision / audit event.
Allison Grant (author): Added example query + notes; full audit-event join is a follow-up once eval_id is threaded into the controller.

Approvals: Miles Thornton approved. Ravi Menon approved with nit fixes. Sergio Costa approved.
merge_outcome: Merged via squash into main by Miles Thornton. Squash commit: "region-health: structured logging for evaluation path". No rollback required.
